newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Moody's upgrades Shell Australia ratings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Moody's upgrades Shell Australia ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it has upgraded Shell Australia Ltd's long-term ratings, lifting its Euronotes and Eurobonds to Aa3 from A1, concluding a rating review undertaken in February this year.
Shell Australia, an integrated resources company, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell.
Moody's said the upgrade reflected Shell Australia's improved core asset focus, its strong financial position, and a rising upstream exploration and production profile in the medium to longer term.
Shell Australia had exited the cyclical and low-return metals and chemicals businesses.
It was now focused on upstream petroleum investments in the North West Shelf and the Timor Sea, on refining and product marketing in Australia, and on building its coal business.

"In particular, Shell Australia has registered considerable offshore success in 1995/96 via direct exploration and its Woodside investment, indicating the potential for major growth in oil, condensate and natural gas reserves in the medium-term," Moody's said.
Shell Australia has a 34 percent stake in Woodside Petroleum Ltd, the operator of the North West Shelf oil and gas project offshore Western Australia.
Moody's said Shell Australia also had reduced debt, and was expected to maintain conservative financial policies and a strong balance sheet and cash flow protection measures.
The upgrading affected about A$675 million of debt securities, Moody's said.
